The **Mean Value Theorem (MVT)** is the one about derivatives and slopes.\n\n**The Theorem in Plain English:**\nIf a function is smooth and continuous on an interval, there is at least one point in the middle where the **instantaneous speed** (derivative) matches the **average speed** over the whole trip.\n\nMathematically: $f\u0027(c) \u003d \\frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}$\n\nHere are problems categorized by how MVT is applied, from basic calculations to logic puzzles.\n\n---\n\n### Level 1: \"Find the Value\" (Calculations)\nThese are standard homework problems to ensure you can perform the mechanism of the theorem.\n\n**Problem 1: The Basic Polynomial**\nGiven the function $f(x) \u003d x^3 - x$ on the interval $[0, 2]$.\nFind all values of $c$ in the interval $(0, 2)$ that satisfy the conclusion of the Mean Value Theorem.\n*(Hint: Calculate the average slope between $x\u003d0$ and $x\u003d2$, then set the derivative $3x^2 - 1$ equal to that number.)*\n\n**Problem 2: The Natural Log**\nConsider $f(x) \u003d \\ln(x)$ on the interval $[1, e]$.\nFind the value $c$ such that the tangent line at $c$ is parallel to the secant line connecting the endpoints.\n\n---\n\n### Level 2: The \"Speeding Ticket\" (Real World)\nMVT is the mathematical justification for average-speed traffic cameras.\n\n**Problem 3: The Turnpike Problem**\nA driver enters a toll road at 1:00 PM. They exit the toll road at a station 80 miles away at 2:15 PM. The speed limit is 60 mph.\nUse the Mean Value Theorem to prove that the driver was speeding at some point during the trip, even if the police never saw them do it.\n*(Hint: Convert 2 hours and 15 minutes to a decimal or fraction of hours, find the average velocity, and apply MVT).*\n\n**Problem 4: The Drag Race**\nTwo cars start a race at the same time and finish the race in a tie.\nProve that at some point during the race, the two cars had the exact same velocity.\n*(Hint: Let $h(t) \u003d f(t) - g(t)$ where $f$ and $g$ are the position functions of the cars. Note that $h(Start) \u003d 0$ and $h(Finish) \u003d 0$. This is actually Rolle\u0027s Theorem, a special case of MVT).*\n\n---\n\n### Level 3: Proving \"Uniqueness\" (Roots)\nThis is a very common exam application. You usually use IVT to prove a root *exists*, and MVT (specifically Rolle\u0027s Theorem) to prove only *one* exists.\n\n**Problem 5: One Root Only**\nShow that the equation $f(x) \u003d x^3 + x + 1 \u003d 0$ has **exactly one** real root.\n*   **Step A (IVT):** Show that a root exists (try $f(-1)$ and $f(0)$).\n*   **Step B (MVT/Rolle\u0027s):** Assume there are two roots, $a$ and $b$.         "text": "Got it. The **Mean Value Theorem (MVT)** is the one about derivatives and slopes.\n\n**The Theorem in Plain English:**\nIf a function is smooth and continuous on an interval, there is at least one point in"
      }, {
        "text": " the middle where the **instantaneous speed** (derivative) matches the **average speed** over the whole trip.\n\nMathemat"
      }, {
        "text": "ically: $f\u0027(c) \u003d \\frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}$"
      }, {
        "text": "\n\nHere are problems categorized by how MVT is applied, from basic calculations to logic puzzles.\n\n---\n\n### Level 1"
      }, {
        "text": ": \"Find the Value\" (Calculations)\nThese are standard homework problems to ensure you can perform the mechanism of"
      }, {
        "text": " the theorem.\n\n**Problem 1: The Basic Polynomial**\nGiven the function $f(x) \u003d x^3 -"
      }, {
        "text": " x$ on the interval $[0, 2]$.\nFind all values of $c$ in the interval $(0"
      }, {
        "text": ", 2)$ that satisfy the conclusion of the Mean Value Theorem.\n*(Hint: Calculate the average slope between $"
      }, {
        "text": "x\u003d0$ and $x\u003d2$, then set the derivative $3x^2 - 1$ equal"
      }, {
        "text": " to that number.)*\n\n**Problem 2: The Natural Log**\nConsider $f(x) \u003d \\ln("
      }, {
        "text": "x)$ on the interval $[1, e]$.\nFind the value $c$ such that the tangent line at $"
      }, {
        "text": "c$ is parallel to the secant line connecting the endpoints.\n\n---\n\n### Level 2: The \"Speeding"
      }, {
        "text": " Ticket\" (Real World)\nMVT is the mathematical justification for average-speed traffic cameras.\n\n**Problem 3:"
      }, {
        "text": " The Turnpike Problem**\nA driver enters a toll road at 1:00 PM. They exit the toll road"
      }, {
        "text": " at a station 80 miles away at 2:15 PM. The speed limit is 60 mph"
      }, {
        "text": ".\nUse the Mean Value Theorem to prove that the driver was speeding at some point during the trip, even if the"
      }, {
        "text": " police never saw them do it.\n*(Hint: Convert 2 hours and 15 minutes to a decimal or"
      }, {
        "text": " fraction of hours, find the average velocity, and apply MVT).*\n\n**Problem 4: The Drag Race**\nTwo"
      }, {
        "text": " cars start a race at the same time and finish the race in a tie.\nProve that at some point during the race, the"
      }, {
        "text": " two cars had the exact same velocity.\n*(Hint: Let $h(t) \u003d f(t) - g("
      }, {
        "text": "t)$ where $f$ and $g$ are the position functions of the cars. Note that $h(Start"
      }, {
        "text": ") \u003d 0$ and $h(Finish) \u003d 0$. This is actually Rolle\u0027s Theorem, a"
      }, {
        "text": " special case of MVT).*\n\n---\n\n### Level 3: Proving \"Uniqueness\" (Roots)\nThis is"
      }, {
        "text": " a very common exam application. You usually use IVT to prove a root *exists*, and MVT (specifically Rolle\u0027s"
      }, {
        "text": " Theorem) to prove only *one* exists.\n\n**Problem 5: One Root Only**\nShow that the equation $"
      }, {
        "text": "f(x) \u003d x^3 + x + 1 \u003d 0$ has **exactly one** real root.\n"
      }, {
        "text": "*   **Step A (IVT):** Show that a root exists (try $f(-1)$ and $f("
      }, {
        "text": "0)$).\n*   **Step B (MVT/Rolle\u0027s):** Assume there are two roots"
      }, {
        "text": ", $a$ and $b$. Apply MVT to show that this would require $f\u0027(c) \u003d 0$. Then"
      }, {
        "text": " look at the actual derivative of the function—is it ever zero?\n\n**Problem 6: The Cosine Intersection"
      }, {
        "text": "**\nProve that the equation $\\cos(x) \u003d 2x$ has exactly one solution.\n\n---\n\n### Level"
      }, {
        "text": " 4: Proving Inequalities\nThis is the most elegant use of MVT. Instead of manipulating algebra, you treat"
      }, {
        "text": " an expression as a slope.\n\n**Problem 7: The Sine Inequality**\nProve that $|\\sin(a)"
      }, {
        "text": " - \\sin(b)| \\le |a - b|$ for all real numbers $a$ and $b$."
      }, {
        "text": "\n*(Hint: Rearrange the inequality to look like $\\left| \\frac{\\sin a - \\sin b}{a"
      }, {
        "text": " - b} \\right| \\le 1$. Realize the left side is the definition of the MVT for $"
      }, {
        "text": "f(x)\u003d\\sin x$. What is the maximum value of the derivative of sine?)*\n\n**Problem 8"
      }, {
        "text": ": Bounding the Square Root**\nUse the Mean Value Theorem to prove that for $x \u003e 0$:\n$$ \\"
      }, {
        "text": "sqrt{1+x} \u003c 1 + \\frac{x}{2} $$\n*(Hint: Consider the function $f"
      }, {
        "text": "(t) \u003d \\sqrt{t}$ on the interval $[1, 1+x]$.)*\n\n---\n\n###"
      }, {
        "text": " Level 5: Conceptual / Abstract\n**Problem 9: The Bounded Derivative**\nSuppose $f$ is continuous"
      }, {
        "text": " and differentiable on real numbers, and suppose that for all $x$, $f\u0027(x) \\le 5$."
      }, {
        "text": "\nIf $f(0) \u003d 4$, what is the largest possible value for $f(3)$?\n*("
      }, {
        "text": "Hint: Use the formula $f\u0027(c) \u003d \\frac{f(3) - f(0)}{3 - "
      }, {
        "text": "0}$ and solve for $f(3)$).*\n\n**Problem 10: The Constant Function**\nUse"
      }, {
        "text": " the Mean Value Theorem to prove that if $f\u0027(x) \u003d 0$ for all $x$ in an"
      }, {
        "text": " interval $(a, b)$, then $f(x)$ must be a constant function on that interval.\n*(This"
      }, {
        "text": " seems obvious, but MVT is the actual proof: Pick any two points $x_1$ and $x_2$. If"
      }, {
        "text": " the derivative is always 0, what does that force the numerator $f(x_2) - f(x_"
      }, {
        "text": "1)$ to be?)*"
      }, {

      }]
